item.lead: Two imports near the top of the file name the two worlds the app lives in. One is `asyncio`, which handles each incoming request. The other is a pair, `threading` and `concurrent.futures`, which supply threads for SQLite, which blocks while it works. Look at those lines, then at the setting that says how many such threads exist by default.
item.follow: You saw two worlds: asyncio carries the request, and a small pool of threads, three by default, does the blocking SQLite work. Next, we look at how the app turns these settings into configuration, databases and shared state.

perform.line: /explain Why does the app import asyncio alongside threading and futures, and what does a default of 3 SQL threads mean? Show it on the imports at lines 3, 23 and 27 and the setting for threads in the pool for executing SQLite queries (lines 228-232). The reader already knows: the top of the file is a parts list. Do not cover: templates, settings handling, databases, shared state. Afterwards the reader can point at those imports and the default of 3, and say asyncio runs the request while a thread pool runs blocking SQLite work.
